current_example.problem: Use trial and error to compute the multiplicative inverse of $8$ modulo $15.$
current_example.worked_solution:
The multiplicative inverse of $8$ modulo $15,$ denoted $8^{-1},$ is the number $x$ such that

$$
8 \cdot x \equiv 1 \quad (\textrm{mod}\:15).
$$

Note that since $\text{gcd}(8,15) = 1,$ an inverse element exists and is unique up to congruence modulo $15.$

Since the modulus $n=15$ is small, we can find the inverse $x$ by computing exponents of $8$ (modulo $15$) until we get a result of $1\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{8}^{2} & ≡8\cdot 8≡64≡4\cdot 15+4≡4 &  & (\text{mod}\,15) \\ {8}^{3} & ≡8\cdot 4≡32≡2\cdot 15+2≡2 &  & (\text{mod}\,15) \\ {8}^{4} & ≡8\cdot 2≡16≡15+1≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,15)\end{aligned}
$$

So, $8 \cdot 2 \equiv 1 \, (\textrm{mod} \:15).$ Therefore, the multiplicative inverse of $8$ modulo $15$ is $\bbox[3pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}2}.$
